data.cultural_impact: Dyumana is a Sanskrit name with deep cultural roots in Hindu mythology. The name is associated with celestial beings and is the name of the charioteer of the Sun God, Surya. This connection to the sun and celestial beings highlights the importance of light, knowledge, and divinity in Hindu culture. Dyumana is a name that evokes a sense of grandeur and divine power, and is often used as a name for individuals seeking a connection to these ideals.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Dyumana holds deep spiritual significance as the charioteer of the Sun God, Surya. This role symbolizes the connection between light, knowledge, and spiritual growth. The name inspires one to strive for inner radiance and enlightenment, just as the Sun provides light and energy to the world. Additionally, Dyumana is believed to bestow the blessings of the Sun God, bringing prosperity, happiness, and wisdom to those who bear the name.

historical_references.reference: The Hindu sage Dyumana is mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic. He is described as an expert in the science of astronomy and astrology.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is a Sanskrit epic poem consisting of 100,000 verses, composed between 400 BCE and 200 BCE. Dyumana is a sage who advises Yudhishthira, the eldest of the five Pandava brothers, on astronomical matters.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Dyumana can be found in the Puranas, a collection of ancient Indian texts. He is considered the chief among the seven rishis or sages who were born from the mind of the god Brahma.
historical_references.context: Puranas are a set of eighteen major Sanskrit texts and numerous minor texts, dating from between 400 CE and 1200 CE. Dyumana is revered as one of the seven great sages born from the mind of the creator god Brahma.
